successCriteria.description: The LeaveRequest entity is exported from src/modules/leave-request/leave-request.model.ts with exactly the canonical fields (id, employeeId, leavePolicyId, startDate, endDate, reason, status, approvedBy, approvedAt, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, createdAt, updatedAt) and the status field is typed as LeaveRequestStatus imported from src/shared/types/leave-request-status.enum.ts; nullable fields (reason, approvedBy, approvedAt, cancelledBy, cancelledAt) use the nullable union types matching the reconciled architecture.

The ILeaveRequestRepository interface declares all eight required operations: findById, findByEmployeeId, findByStatus, findByEmployeeAndStatus, findPendingForManager, save, update, and updateStatus — each with a signature consistent with the sibling repositories (single-entity lookups return the entity or null, collection lookups return an array, save returns the persisted entity).

PgLeaveRequestRepository implements ILeaveRequestRepository and performs all database access exclusively through the shared pool imported from src/shared/db/connection.ts (GP-001 repository pattern); no inline SQL or direct pg calls exist outside the repository class.

findPendingForManager(managerId) returns leave requests whose employee's managerId equals the given managerId and whose status is a pending state (DRAFT or SUBMITTED), enabling the manager approval workflow; the query joins or filters against the employee reporting line so only direct reports' requests are returned.

updateStatus(id, status, metadata) atomically transitions the request's status and stamps the corresponding actor/timestamp fields from metadata (e.g. approvedBy/approvedAt on APPROVED, cancelledBy/cancelledAt on CANCELLED) in a single UPDATE, returning the updated entity or null when the id does not exist.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/leave-request/ covering the model field shape and every repository method (findById, findByEmployeeId, findByStatus, findByEmployeeAndStatus, findPendingForManager, save, update, updateStatus) with the db pool mocked, including the not-found (null/empty) and happy-path branches — matching the test structure of the sibling leave-balance tests.
The module compiles under strict TypeScript (npm run build / tsc --noEmit) with no implicit any and no type errors, and the Jest suite (npx jest) passes for the new leave-request tests.

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high); the mapRow helper and all query result handling must type-cast from Record<string, unknown> as the sibling repositories do.

All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / HARNESS.json no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical); PgLeaveRequestRepository is the only component that issues SQL, using the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts.

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts) per ARCHITECTURE.md dependency rules; the leave-request model may import Employee and LeavePolicy reference types via their module index, and LeaveRequestStatus via the shared types path, but must not reach into sibling module internals.
No circular dependencies between modules (ARCHITECTURE.md); leave-request may depend on employee, leave-policy, and shared-types but those modules must not import back from leave-request.

Repository methods that must be atomic with a caller's transaction accept an optional PoolClient as their last parameter and use `const db = client ?? pool` (the optional-client pattern documented in ARCHITECTURE.md); updateStatus and any method participating in the approval balance-deduction transaction must support this so Phase 9 can run them inside the same unit of work as incrementUsedDays.

No unhandled promise rejections (GP-006); all async repository methods must propagate errors via returned/rejected promises without swallowing them, consistent with the sibling repository implementations.
outOfScope: LeaveRequest service, controller, and routes (Phase 9) — no business-rule enforcement (submit/approve/reject/cancel workflow, balance deduction, minimum-notice validation, RBAC) belongs in this phase; the repository is a pure persistence layer.
Audit logging of leave request state transitions (GP-002 / Phase 10) — the repository must not write audit records; that is the service layer's responsibility in later phases.
Input validation at API boundaries (GP-003) and RBAC enforcement (GP-005) — these are controller/middleware concerns (Phase 9), not repository concerns; the repository trusts its callers.

Business-day counting utility (src/shared/utils/business-days.ts) and balance sufficiency checks — these are service-layer concerns (Phase 9); the repository persists dates as-is without computing day counts.

Database migrations / DDL for the leave_requests table — this phase creates TypeScript model and repository code only; the SQL schema is documented in the reconciled architecture but migrations are not part of this phase's deliverables.

ambiguities.description: The `updateStatus(id, status, metadata)` signature's `metadata` parameter shape is unspecified. It must carry the actor and timestamp for the transition (approvedBy/approvedAt for APPROVED, cancelledBy/cancelledAt for CANCELLED), but whether it is a typed object, a Partial<LeaveRequest>, or a generic record is left to the code agent. The risk is that Phase 9's service expects a specific shape.
options: metadata is a Partial<LeaveRequest> containing only the actor/timestamp fields relevant to the transition
metadata is a dedicated typed object { approvedBy?, approvedAt?, cancelledBy?, cancelledAt?, reason? }
metadata is a generic Record<string, unknown> the repository maps onto columns

ambiguities.description: findPendingForManager(managerId) must return requests for a manager's direct reports in a pending state, but "pending" is not precisely defined. The LeaveRequestStatus enum has DRAFT and SUBMITTED as pre-decision states; APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED are terminal. Whether DRAFT requests (not yet submitted) should appear in a manager's pending queue is ambiguous — a manager typically only acts on SUBMITTED requests.
options: pending = SUBMITTED only (manager acts on submitted requests, not drafts)
pending = DRAFT or SUBMITTED (any non-terminal state)
pending = SUBMITTED, and DRAFT is excluded because the employee has not yet submitted

ambiguities.description: findPendingForManager requires resolving the employee reporting line (employees whose managerId = managerId). The leave_requests table has no manager_id column, so the repository must either join to the employees table or the service must pre-resolve report IDs. Whether the repository is permitted to JOIN across tables (crossing the employee module's data) or must receive pre-resolved employee IDs is an architectural boundary question.
options: repository JOINs leave_requests to employees on employee_id where employees.manager_id = $1 (single query)
repository receives a list of employee IDs and filters leave_requests by employee_id IN (...) (no cross-table join, service resolves reports)
repository exposes findByEmployeeIds(ids[]) and the service composes findPendingForManager from employee lookups

entityInvariants.invariant: The status field must always be one of the LeaveRequestStatus enum values (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED); the entity's status lifecycle follows DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED, though the repository itself does not enforce transition legality (that is the service's job in Phase 9) — it only persists whatever status it is given.

The actor/timestamp fields are coupled to the terminal status: approvedBy and approvedAt are non-null only when status is APPROVED; cancelledBy and cancelledAt are non-null only when status is CANCELLED; when status is DRAFT or SUBMITTED these four fields are null. The repository's updateStatus must stamp the correct pair for the target status and leave the others null.

startDate must not be after endDate (a leave request spans a non-negative date range); while the repository does not validate this (validation is an API-boundary concern), the entity shape must allow the dates to be compared and the persisted row must preserve both endpoints exactly.

employeeId and leavePolicyId are non-nullable foreign keys referencing employees.id and leave_policies.id respectively (per the reconciled SQL schema); a LeaveRequest cannot exist without an owning employee and a governing policy. The repository persists these as required columns.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the LeaveRequest with the given id, or null when no row matches; never throws on not-found. Errors from the database propagate as rejected promises (GP-006).
Returns an array of all leave requests for the employee (possibly empty); never returns null. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns an array of leave requests matching the given LeaveRequestStatus (possibly empty); never null. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns an array of leave requests for the employee filtered by status (possibly empty); never null. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns an array of pending leave requests submitted by the manager's direct reports (possibly empty); never null. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.

Inserts the request and returns the persisted entity (with any database-generated values); a unique-constraint violation or other DB error propagates as a rejected promise. Not idempotent — calling twice with the same id attempts a duplicate insert.

Merges the partial onto the existing row (read-then-write, matching the sibling repositories), sets updatedAt to the current time, and returns the updated entity or null when the id does not exist. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.

Atomically sets the status and stamps the corresponding actor/timestamp fields from metadata in a single UPDATE, returning the updated entity or null when the id does not exist. Must accept an optional PoolClient so Phase 9 can run it inside the same transaction as the balance deduction. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveRequest entity's status field must be typed as LeaveRequestStatus imported from this exact file (not a re-declared string union); the enum members DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED are the only valid status values.

The PgLeaveRequestRepository must follow the same structural pattern as PgEmployeeRepository: import pool from the shared db connection, use a private mapRow(row: Record<string, unknown>) helper to convert snake_case DB columns to camelCase entity fields, use parameterized queries ($1, $2, ...) with a values array, and have update perform a read-then-write merge that sets updatedAt to new Date().

The optional-client transaction pattern (const db = client ?? pool; optional PoolClient as last parameter) established by PgLeaveBalanceRepository.incrementUsedDays must be applied to updateStatus (and any method that Phase 9 will call inside the approval transaction) so the status transition and balance deduction can share one unit of work.

The LeaveRequest model must follow the same module-structure convention as LeaveBalance: an exported interface for the entity, reference types (Pick<Employee,'id'> / Pick<LeavePolicy,'id'>) imported via the sibling module index.ts for foreign-key documentation, and the status enum imported from the shared types path — not redeclared locally.

The leave-request repository tests must match the established test pattern: jest.mock('shared/db/connection') with a mocked pool.query, a makeRequest() factory and makeRow() snake_case mapper, beforeEach mockReset, and per-method describe blocks covering found / not-found branches — using the moduleDirectories:['node_modules','src'] import paths (e.g. 'modules/leave-request', 'shared/db/connection').

The LeaveRequest entity attributes must match the reconciled architecture exactly: id, employeeId, leavePolicyId, startDate (Date), endDate (Date), reason (string | undefined), status (LeaveRequestStatus), approvedBy (string | null), approvedAt (Date | null), cancelledBy (string | null), cancelledAt (Date | null), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date) — including the nullable unions for reason and the actor/timestamp fields.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveRequest.status is typed as LeaveRequestStatus from this enum; the repository's findByStatus and updateStatus operations consume its values.

LeaveRequest.employeeId, approvedBy, and cancelledBy reference employees.id; findPendingForManager must resolve the manager→direct-reports relationship through the employee module's data (managerId field). The model imports Employee reference types via the employee module index.
LeaveRequest.leavePolicyId references leave_policies.id; the model imports LeavePolicy reference types via the leave-policy module index for foreign-key type documentation.
